intro: Coventry City have re-signed midfielder Gustavo Hamer from Sheffield United on what the club described as a "long-term" contract, with the transfer carried out for an undisclosed fee, BBC Sport reports. The move sees Hamer return to the club where he previously played, strengthening Coventry's midfield options.

sections.heading: What the transfer entails
sections.text:
According to BBC Sport, Gustavo Hamer has moved from Sheffield United back to Coventry City on a long-term contract. The fee involved in the transaction has not been made public. Re-signing a player in this manner typically indicates the acquiring club views the player as part of its medium- to long-term plans, and Coventry will be hoping Hamer can contribute consistently in the seasons ahead.

The term "long-term" in transfer announcements generally refers to a multi-year agreement, though the exact duration and any contract clauses have not been disclosed in this case. An undisclosed fee means the clubs have chosen not to reveal financial details to the public; this is a common practice in football transfers.

sections.text:
Gustavo Hamer is a midfielder who has previously represented Coventry City before spending time with Sheffield United, and he now returns to Coventry as reported by BBC Sport. Coventry City is an English club with an established presence in the professional league system and a loyal fan base; the club has regularly sought to build squads capable of competing in the divisions they inhabit. Sheffield United are another well-known English club, traditionally playing their home matches at Bramall Lane and competing in the upper tiers of the domestic game.

For Coventry supporters, re-signing a familiar midfielder can provide an immediate boost in both squad continuity and dressing-room cohesion. For Sheffield United, transferring a player on to his former club could be part of a wider squad reshaping process, though specifics have not been provided by either club in the BBC Sport item.

analysis:
This signing, as reported by BBC Sport, suggests Coventry City are prioritising experience and familiarity in midfield by bringing back a former player. Reacquiring a known quantity can reduce the adaptation period that new signings often require and can help a manager implement tactical plans more quickly. Analysts might view the undisclosed nature of the fee and the "long-term" label as an attempt by both clubs to manage expectations and maintain negotiating flexibility in future transfer windows.

From a squad-building perspective, adding a midfielder with previous ties to the club can also be a signal to supporters that the club is focused on assembling a competitive group while balancing financial considerations. How this move fits into Coventry's overall transfer strategy will become clearer as the club announces further signings or departures.
